title: Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee: pay only for AI product visuals that pass
summary: Learn all about how Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee puts product fidelity in the contract. You agree pass/fail criteria, and pay only for AI product visuals that pass.
body_markdown:
*Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee is a contractual commitment that lets enterprise teams pay only for AI product images that meet pre-agreed product-fidelity criteria. Photoroom tests the platform on your catalog before you sign, co-writes pass/fail criteria into the contract, checks every output against those criteria with a proprietary fidelity model, and regenerates any image that misses at no cost to you. It covers factual product accuracy, such as altered colors, ingredients, or shapes, rather than creative preferences like background tone, and it is available to food and fashion teams as a yearly-contract.*


---


For enterprise teams, improving content quality and consistency is one of the biggest reasons to invest in new AI tools. In the March 2026[Photoroom B2B Enterprise Buyer Survey](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/fidelity-gap-ai-product-photography) , 75% of leaders said it was what started their search for new solutions.


But for product visuals, quality alone isn't enough. Enterprises also need to trust that AI-generated product images accurately represent the products they're meant to sell. When asked about their biggest concern with AI-generated product images, 37% of leaders cited the risk of inaccurate or misrepresented visuals.


That creates a problem the industry has largely left e‑commerce teams to solve. When an AI output is wrong, the cost doesn't stop at regenerating the image. Someone has to spot the error, determine whether it is acceptable, send it back through the workflow, and pay for another generation. The model produced the output, but your business absorbs the risk.


The[Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee](https://www.photoroom.com/inside-photoroom/photoroom-launches-the-first-contractual-ai-visual-guarantee-backed-by-a-proprietary-fidelity-model) changes that equation. Instead of asking your business to carry the cost of AI's failures, Photoroom puts a commitment behind the output and gives you a clearer standard for what happens when the system gets it wrong.


## **What is the Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee?**


The[Enterprise Guarantee](https://www.photoroom.com/enterprise/guarantee) is a contractual commitment by Photoroom that allows e‑commerce teams with large image volumes and specific fidelity requirements to pay only for image outputs that meet pre-agreed product-fidelity criteria.


**Here’s what the Enterprise Guarantee covers:**


-


**It defines failure before production.** With the Guarantee, your team agrees on image pass/fail criteria upfront, and Photoroom fixes or regenerates outputs that don't meet those criteria, so that you only pay for outputs that pass.


-


**It applies to factual product accuracy,** covering altered colors, food ingredients, shapes, and other inaccurate details a buyer would notice on a listing, rather than subjective creative preferences like lighting direction or background tone, which aren't fidelity failures.


-


**It usually layers onto**[Visual Agents](https://www.photoroom.com/enterprise/visual-agents) . Most enterprise customers with specific fidelity requirements add it to an existing Visual Agents workflow, where it applies fidelity criteria tailored to their catalog and puts a contractual commitment behind every output


It's a shift from "best-effort" AI output to a contracted outcome, which matters because an AI-edited product image that changes a product's details slows buying decision, drives up return rates, and pulls down gross merchandise value (GMV), on top of the editing cost your team pays to correct it.


Consumers increasingly expect businesses to take responsibility for the accuracy of the product information they see. In Photoroom's[State of GenAI in Marketplaces 2026 report](https://www.photoroom.com/industry-trends/state-of-genai-in-marketplaces-2026) , 78% of UK consumers said marketplaces should ensure product listings are accurate and trustworthy. And 51% said they would switch to another marketplace with more accurate product images.


As Anne-Claire Baschet, Chief Data & AI Officer for Agentic Commerce at Mirakl, the enterprise marketplace platform, puts it, "People buy pictures and receive products. You can't afford to have any modification in the color, shape, or other product details."


For teams processing thousands to millions of images, the Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee turns that expectation into the standard we check every output against.


### **Who is the Enterprise Guarantee for?**


The Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee is for[enterprise teams](https://www.photoroom.com/enterprise) producing large volumes of product visuals with strict product-fidelity requirements. It is currently designed for teams in food and fashion, with eligibility determined by your brand’s catalog, production scope, and volume.


**The guarantee is particularly relevant to:**


-


**Food businesses** where an altered ingredient or product detail can misrepresent what your brand is selling.


-


**Fashion businesses** where changes to color, shape, patterns, or garment details can make an image inaccurate.


-


**Teams processing high-volume catalogs with strict fidelity criteria** who need contractual assurance that outputs stay true to the product.


-


**Teams already operating with Photoroom’s Visual Agents** , since the Guarantee is an optional add-on layered on top of an existing[Visual Agents workflow](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/automate-product-image-quality-control-enterprise-scale) .


If your team integrates an AI-powered workflow to produce product visuals at scale, and you need the platform, rather than your internal team, to take responsibility when those visuals fail your agreed product-fidelity standards, the Enterprise Guarantee is the commitment layer that enables that. We check your sample images in a feasibility test before you commit, so you only sign once we've proven it works for your catalog.


## **How does Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee work?**


The Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee works as a fully managed, end-to-end contractual commitment: we test the platform on your catalog before you commit, agree pass/fail criteria in the contract, check every output against those criteria, and regenerate any miss until it passes.


**Here are the four stages of the Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee:**


1.


**Test before you commit:** We check the platform against your sample images before you sign a contract, and onboarding starts only if the results pass.


2.


**Agree on the pass/fail criteria:** You and our team co-write pass/fail criteria from your product fidelity standards, and the contract locks them in before we generate a single production image.


3.


**Generate and check:** Our proprietary fidelity model checks every output against your criteria for product fidelity and technical quality, so that your team doesn’t handle outputs that fail.


4.


**The system regenerates failed outputs:** When an output fails the agreed criteria, we regenerate it until it meets your standard, and you pay only for the outputs you accept.


Every step depends on the criteria in your contract, which draw the line between a fidelity miss and a creative call. Complex generations like[AI Fashion Models](https://www.photoroom.com/api/virtual-model) or patterned garments can take more than one retry to meet your criteria, and we cover those attempts. Photoroom manages the full loop from feasibility test to accepted output.


The four steps of Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee, from feasibility test to regeneration of failed outputs. Regenerated images go back through the same fidelity check.


### **What qualifies for regeneration under Photoroom's Enterprise Guarantee (and what doesn't)?**


Under the Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee, an output qualifies for regeneration when it changes the product against your agreed product-fidelity criteria. Aesthetic choices outside those criteria don't qualify for regeneration.


For example, if the system produces the wrong color of your tomato sauce product, it will regenerate the output. But if it produces a different background color, it doesn’t count as a miss because background colors are not products.


**The table below shows where the line sits in practice, matching each type of fidelity miss with the creative call it's often mistaken for:**


Area Qualifies for regeneration Doesn't qualify for regeneration


Color Wrong product color A different background tone


Product contents An added, removed, or missing product feature A square plate instead of a round one


Shape A distorted product or garment shape A pose you'd have framed differently


Your contract ultimately decides what qualifies and what doesn’t. Because you co-write the pass/fail criteria before production starts, every regeneration decision is measured against a written standard your team helped set, and you can resolve disputes against the contract rather than vague standards.


Putting the criteria in writing also matters because buyers compare generated images with the physical items they receive. "You have to be careful when there are real items," says Olivia Moore, Partner at venture firm Andreessen Horowitz. "Anything you generate has to be substantially similar to what the actual item will be when it's delivered." The criteria in your contract define substantially similar for your catalog, in writing, before production starts.


The Enterprise Guarantee also assumes usable inputs. Low-resolution, badly lit, or placeholder source images fall outside coverage, because our fidelity model checks each output against the product shown in your input, and a bad input doesn’t show what your product truly looks like.


Three product images of a fried rice dish side by side. The original shows the dish on a table. The fidelity miss shows the same dish with cucumber slices added around the plate, an ingredient the product doesn't include. The aesthetic choice shows the unchanged dish on a green background. The added cucumber slices change what the buyer thinks they're ordering, so the image qualifies for regeneration. The green background changes nothing about the product, so it doesn't.


### **How is pay-for-pass different from pay-per-generation?**


Pay-for-pass bills you only for outputs that meet agreed fidelity criteria; pay-per-generation bills for every output the model produces, whether it’s usable or not.


Pay-per-generation is the default billing model for AI image tools, which puts the cost of a failed output on you. If the AI renders the wrong color or alters a food ingredient, you still pay for that generation and absorb the cost of correcting it. The vendor's revenue doesn't depend on whether the image is actually correct, so there's no contractual pressure on quality.


Pay-for-pass is the model the Photoroom Enterprise Guarantee uses. It ties billing to accepted outcomes, shifting the financial risk of an AI imaging error from your team to ours.


**Here’s how pay-per-generation and pay-for-pass compare:**


Area Pay-per-generation Pay-for-pass


What you pay for You pay for every generation, including wrong outputs You pay only for accepted images. Photoroom absorbs failed outputs


Who does the retry work You identify, pay for, and correct the failed outputs Photoroom regenerates misses before they reach your team


Quality gate None. You review after generating Built-in fidelity check before billing


Cost per usable image Your spend covers all generations, so cost per usable image rises with the failure rate Your spend equals accepted images, so cost per usable image stays fixed


Pay-per-generation is a usage model, while pay-for-pass is an outcome guaranteed model. A pay-for-pass model makes cost more predictable for your business; you budget only for accepted visuals, not for rejects and retries. It also allows your team to stop paying for wasted effort. Photoroom provides the Enterprise Guarantee that enables pay-for-pass, so that you shift from paying for production activity to paying for accurate outcomes.


## **How is Photoroom able to guarantee accurate outputs?**


Photoroom can contractually guarantee accurate outputs because we own our entire[visual production stack](https://www.photoroom.com/platform/enterprise-overview) . Our generation models create the image, our proprietary fidelity model scores it against your brief, and our correction process regenerates a miss until it passes. This system ensures that we can control quality end-to-end and stand behind our results instead of relying only on third-party foundation models.


**Here’s why we stand behind outputs:**


1.


**Full-stack ownership:** We build our in-house generation, rating, and image fixing systems.


2.


**Proprietary fidelity evaluation model:** We use a dedicated model to validate every output against your brief and product-fidelity criteria. This is what makes automated scoring at scale possible.


3.


**Automated checking before you pay:** The Fidelity Layer checks every generation and automatically catches fidelity failures before you're billed for output. This is the mechanism that makes the pay-for-pass model work in practice.


4.


**In-house regeneration:** When an output fails, Photoroom regenerates or fixes it internally until it meets the agreed standard, with no retry work returning to your team.


A guarantee is only as strong as the ability to enforce it. Vendors that resell third-party foundation models can’t evaluate or correct what those models produce because they lack the fidelity-checking and correction layer, so their accountability stops at the API.


We designed Photoroom with a system to catch the specific failures that matter for product listings. Photoroom guarantees accurate AI product images because we own the[automated quality-control](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/automate-product-image-quality-control-enterprise-scale) layers that detect when our AI models produce inaccurate images, fix the faulty visuals, and take responsibility for the failed output.
